Innovation Philosophy

We don't treat innovation as a slogan. It's the accumulation of seventeen years of small, disciplined improvements — a better sort line, a faster press, a cleaner extrusion run.

Real innovation in an industrial recycling business rarely looks dramatic from the outside. It looks like investing in the right equipment before you strictly need it, training a workforce that understands why a process matters and not just how to run it, and building structured systems that make quality repeatable at scale rather than accidental.

That's the philosophy behind every division at Skaj & U — from the extrusion line that turns PET bottles into granules, to the press that molds recovered pulp into egg crates, to the sanitation contracts that keep public spaces clean.

Waste Transformation

Every material follows the same disciplined path.

Recovery, sorting, processing and manufacturing aren't separate departments here — they're one continuous system, engineered so nothing that enters it leaves as waste again.

Innovation Framework

Four commitments that shape how we build.

Invest In Equipment

The right press, extruder or baler — bought before it's strictly needed, not after a bottleneck forces it.

Train The Workforce

Every operator understands why a process matters, so quality holds even when volumes scale up.

Structure The System

Repeatable processes, documented steps, and quality checkpoints that make output consistent, not accidental.

Partner Strategically

Long-term relationships with corporations and government agencies that let us plan capacity years ahead.

Manufacturing Technology

The lines that turn recovered material into product.

Extrusion & Granulation

Processing recovered plastic at one tonne every hour.

Sorted PET and nylon feed into our extrusion line, where it's melted, filtered and cut into clean granules — the raw material that becomes the next generation of plastic product.

1 tonne processed every hour
Pulp Molding & Pressing

Twelve bundles of egg crates, molded every hour.

Recovered cardboard and paper pulp is molded under heat and pressure into egg crates — a product used daily by poultry farms and food distributors across the region.

12 bundles produced every hour
Circular Economy Journey

Seventeen years of building the loop, one stage at a time.

2007

Incorporated & Founded

Skaj & U Investment Nigeria Limited is established and incorporated under the Corporate Affairs Commission, Abuja, with recycling and material recovery at its core.

Early Years

Recycling Operations Take Shape

PET bottle recycling, waste sack and nylon recovery are built out, with structured baling and processing lines installed at the Ibadan facility.

Expansion

Manufacturing Enters The Loop

Egg crate manufacturing begins, turning recovered pulp into a market-ready product and closing the loop between recovery and production.

Growth

Sanitation & Agriculture Join The Business

Environmental sanitation contracts with government agencies, and agriculture & livestock farming, extend the company beyond recycling into a fully integrated operation.

Today

Six Divisions, One System

Manufacturing, recycling, sanitation, agriculture, interior solutions and general contracting now operate as one integrated value chain, serving corporate and government clients.

In Development

Cold Room Factory

Our next infrastructure investment — cold storage capacity designed to extend shelf life for agricultural and food-sector partners.

R&D, Material Science & Digital Innovation

Research & Development

Our current flagship R&D effort is the Cold Room Factory — an infrastructure project aimed at extending shelf life for agricultural output, currently in development.

Material Science

Continuous refinement of how we sort, wash and process recovered PET, nylon and pulp — improving output quality and reducing loss at every stage.

Digital Innovation

As our divisions grow, we're investing in the systems needed to track material flow, quality and throughput with the same discipline we apply on the factory floor.

Future Vision

The Cold Room Factory is where our next chapter of innovation is being built.

Cold storage infrastructure will let us extend the shelf life of agricultural output from our own farming operations and from partner producers — reducing post-harvest loss and adding a new layer of value to the circular system we've already built. It's currently in development, and it reflects the same philosophy behind everything else we do: invest in the infrastructure before the need becomes urgent.
